caption: Alerts combines model retirements and performance changes. This demo uses synthetic daily history; every screen reads live HTTP responses from a local LiteLLM proxy.
Open the key spend alert.
This key spent fifty times its established daily baseline. Related request changes appear in the same investigation.
Scroll to Activity.
The charts keep the alert's key and saved date range. You can inspect resources and source signals only when you need them.
Return to Alerts and open the provider latency alert.
The comparison and Activity share the measured provider scope. Grouping shows related observations; it does not claim a proven root cause.
Open the reliability alert.
Here the saved comparison explains the error change and its baseline, with the matching activity below.
Open the traffic alert.
The same investigation view explains a drop in requests against established history.
Open the model retirement alert.
The retirement date, replacement guidance, and recorded usage stay together. Open Migration details for the existing migration workflow.
The migration page preserves affected keys and replacement guidance.
Return to Alerts and open Settings.
Daily monitoring starts with defaults. Settings explains when checks are waiting for history or catching up. Email setup uses the existing Email Settings page.
Edit Unexpected spend.
Change the increase factor when you need a different threshold. Advanced controls stay collapsed, and custom rules can target a particular resource.
Open Notifications.
Alerts link to the same investigations. Updates are collapsed, and the compact resource links remain at the bottom while the content scrolls.
The same Activity charts also live on each resource. Open this key’s Activity tab to continue investigating the exact key and dates.
Team details have Activity too. The chart shows the recorded traffic for this team without rebuilding a filter on the Usage page.
User details reuse the same Activity view and saved dates. The request totals match the live API response.
Model Activity uses the underlying model identity and the same dates. These screens reuse the existing charts; the history shown here is synthetic demo data.
